content: The Tuscan Emergency Medicine Initiative (TEMI) represents a collaborative effort between American emergency physicians from the Harvard Medical Faculty Physicians at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and the Tuscan Ministry of Health. The primary goal of this initiative is to establish standardized training in emergency medicine for the Tuscany region. As of September 2007, the program has successfully trained over 450 emergency physicians in Tuscany. This initiative has the potential to serve as a model for similar training programs in other parts of the world. A comprehensive description of the program has been published in the Annals of Emergency Medicine. Italy currently lacks standardized specialty training in emergency medicine. This absence has resulted in significant variability in the quality of emergency medical care, not only between different hospital emergency departments but also within individual departments. To address this issue, the Tuscan Minister of Health sought to collaborate with emergency medicine specialists from the United States to accelerate the development of this specialty in Tuscany. The collaboration involved multiple entities, including the regional healthcare service, the Tuscan university system, Harvard Medical International, and the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. Administrators integrated emergency medicine training curricula from the European Society of Emergency Medicine and the American Board of Emergency Medicine into a comprehensive program. This program includes a Train-the-Trainers course, a qualification track, and a Master’s degree program. TEMI has three primary objectives: 1. To train future educators in emergency medicine. 2. To ensure that all physicians working in regional hospital emergency departments are appropriately qualified. 3. To establish a regional university Master’s program in emergency medicine, which will serve as a foundation for future specialty training in this field.
